item.text:
**1B.3 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Assessment:** I found no direct 2024 evidence about nuclear custody, warhead safety, or formal command-and-control systems. The closest usable evidence is indirect: Ethiopia’s government and Abiy’s team moved on disaster-response capacity, emergency preparedness, and early nuclear-infrastructure planning with safety/regulatory language. That is supportive, but it is still not the same as demonstrated nuclear command-and-control discipline.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-04-26 | Commission Revamping Disaster Response Works to Address Humanitarian Needs | ENA English | [ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4358046](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4358046) | Ethiopia’s Disaster Risk Management Commission said it was overhauling its structure, policy, staffing, and technology to improve emergency management and response capacity. This is indirect evidence of stronger accident-response discipline and institutional readiness. | 1B.3 |
| 2024-07-01 | Discussion Held with CNNC on Potential Collaboration in Nuclear Energy in Ethiopia | ENA English | [ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4693757](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4693757) | Ethiopian officials discussed peaceful nuclear cooperation with China National Nuclear Corporation, including infrastructure development and human-resource training to support a future nuclear program. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of early institutional groundwork relevant to future nuclear safety and custody controls. | 1B.3, 1B.1 |
| 2024-07-05 | Disaster Policy Instrumental in Mitigating, Responding to Calamities with Own Resources: DRM Commissioner | ENA English | [ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4724392](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4724392) | Officials said the newly ratified disaster-risk policy would help Ethiopia mitigate and respond to natural and manmade calamities using its own resources, with a new structure for the commission. That supports an argument that Abiy’s government was trying to strengthen preventive and response capacity. | 1B.3 |
| 2024-08-17 | Council Vows to Strengthen Disaster Emergency Response Activities in Ethiopia | ENA English | [ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4989768](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4989768) | The disaster-risk council said Ethiopia needed a more effective emergency-preparedness system to manage future accidents and directed stronger prevention and timely information-sharing after deadly landslides and floods. This is relevant as general accident-prevention evidence, though not nuclear-specific. | 1B.3 |
| 2024-11-03 | Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia | ENA English | [ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124) | The state-of-emergency proclamation centralized coercive authority to address internal threats and authorized an operation command to issue directives. This is not evidence of safety safeguards; if anything, it shows reliance on emergency control structures rather than transparent custody or risk-prevention governance. | 1B.3, 7A.* |

**Search gap**

- I looked directly for 2024 evidence of nuclear command-and-control discipline, custody, or accident-prevention safeguards.
- I found no source showing Abiy personally strengthening nuclear custody systems, reactor safety regulation, or weapons-related command-and-control, and no evidence that Ethiopia had an operational nuclear arsenal in 2024.
- So the evidentiary record for this lens is mostly indirect and low-specificity.

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported reading: weak-to-moderate positive evidence on general emergency preparedness and early nuclear-governance buildout.
- No direct evidence of nuclear command-and-control discipline.
- No strong opposing evidence specifically about unsafe nuclear custody; the main negative context is the broader reliance on emergency powers amid internal conflict.
